token_estimate_method: file bytes / 4; approximate, not measured by a tokenizer

rules: Open exactly one entry skill (ctf-playbook) per challenge.
Open exactly one router for the selected category.
Do not open a depth skill before the first probe has produced a signal, unless the input format itself is unrecognised.
Open one depth reference file, not a whole depth directory.
If the router and the depth skill disagree, the router wins and the disagreement is recorded as an observation.
Never open a second category's router to 'check'; re-run tools/skill_select.py instead.

layers.entry: Classifies the challenge and manages contest time. Never solves.
layers.router: Maps one observed signal to one bug class and one cheapest probe. Short by design.
layers.depth: Large technique corpus. Opened only to answer a specific question the router raised.
layers.reference: A single file inside a depth or router directory.

use_when: a new challenge starts and the category is not yet fixed
several challenges compete for time in a timed contest
do_not_use_when: the category is already established by ctf.py or by given source
a probe is already running and only needs interpretation

use_when: an HTTP target, a web framework, or web source code is supplied
a route, request parameter, cookie, or template is under discussion
do_not_use_when: the artifact is a binary, capture, or ciphertext with no HTTP surface
the bug class is already confirmed by a probe: open that depth skill instead

use_when: an ELF/PE binary accepts input and the goal is memory corruption
a crash, checksec output, or libc version is part of the evidence
do_not_use_when: the binary only has to be understood, not corrupted: use rev-triage
the binary is firmware to be unpacked: use rev-triage firmware reference

use_when: a binary, bytecode, managed assembly, packed sample, or firmware image must be understood
a check function or embedded algorithm has to be replicated
do_not_use_when: a memory-corruption primitive is the goal: use pwn-binary-triage
the sample is live malware with C2 behaviour: use ctf-malware

use_when: ciphertext, a modulus, a nonce, a key, or a hash is supplied
a custom encryption routine must be broken rather than reversed
do_not_use_when: the algorithm only has to be recovered from a binary: use rev-triage first
the data is an encoding rather than encryption: use ctf-misc

use_when: a PCAP, disk image, memory dump, log set, document, or media file is supplied
something is believed to be hidden inside a container format
do_not_use_when: the capture is only used to read a protocol you already understand
the sample must be executed or decompiled: use rev-triage

use_when: the challenge supplies a name, handle, photo, domain, or document and the answer lives in public sources
do_not_use_when: the challenge has a reachable target to probe: OSINT is not recon for an owned host
you would query a real person's data outside the challenge's stated scope

use_when: an LLM/chatbot endpoint, a model file, or an embedded/IoT firmware or protocol capture is supplied
do_not_use_when: the model file is only a pickle to be weaponised: use web-deserialization
the firmware is a plain binary to reverse: use rev-triage

use_when: a request value is concatenated into a query, or a probe produced an SQL error, boolean delta, or timing delta
do_not_use_when: no query-shaped sink has been observed in source or response

use_when: the server fetches a URL the request controls, or a bot/renderer visits a supplied address
do_not_use_when: the fetch target is fixed in source and not influenced by the request

use_when: a request value is rendered by a template engine, or an arithmetic marker evaluated
do_not_use_when: the marker was reflected literally: that is XSS-shaped, not SSTI

use_when: a marker reaches an HTML, attribute, JS, or DOM context, and a bot or admin view can fire it
do_not_use_when: nothing consumes the injected markup: without a viewer there is no flag path

use_when: object identifiers appear in a path, body, or token and ownership may not be enforced
do_not_use_when: only one identity is available: an ownership claim needs two

use_when: the app stores a supplied file and something later reads, renders, or executes it
do_not_use_when: the stored file is never served or parsed again

use_when: a session token, JWT, signed cookie, reset flow, or role boundary decides access to the flag
do_not_use_when: the boundary is per-object rather than per-role: use web-idor

use_when: a serialized blob crosses a trust boundary, or source calls a deserializer on request data or on a supplied model file
do_not_use_when: the blob is signed and the key is unknown and unreachable

use_when: an arbitrary or partial file read has been proven and source, config, or the flag path must be located
do_not_use_when: the read primitive is still a hypothesis: prove it from the router first

use_when: control of the instruction pointer is proven and NX forces code reuse
do_not_use_when: the offset or the crash is not yet established
skills.unlock_signals: rop|ret2libc|gadget|nx enabled|pop rdi|no pie|leak libc|instruction pointer

use_when: the web depth skill did not contain the specific variant, filter bypass, or CVE the evidence points to
do_not_use_when: a narrower web-* depth skill covers the class: open that instead
never read the whole directory; open one named file
skills.manual_gate: a narrower web-* depth skill did not contain the needed variant

use_when: the primitive is known and a specific heap, kernel, format-string, or sandbox technique is needed
do_not_use_when: the crash has not been reproduced yet
never read the whole directory; open one named file
skills.manual_gate: the crash is reproduced and a named heap/kernel/format technique is needed

use_when: a specific language runtime, packer, VM obfuscator, or anti-analysis trick has been identified
do_not_use_when: static triage has not yet named the runtime or the packer
never read the whole directory; open one named file
skills.manual_gate: the runtime or packer is named and a specific technique is needed

use_when: the primitive and its parameters are collected and a named attack has to be implemented
do_not_use_when: parameters such as n, e, c, nonce, or key size are still unknown
never read the whole directory; open one named file
skills.manual_gate: the primitive parameters are collected and a named attack must be implemented

use_when: the artifact type is identified and a container-specific extraction is required
do_not_use_when: file/strings/metadata triage has not been run
never read the whole directory; open one named file
skills.manual_gate: the artifact type is identified and a container-specific extraction is required

use_when: the challenge is a jail, an encoding chain, a game or VM, a DNS puzzle, or a programming constraint
do_not_use_when: the challenge fits a named category: misc is the last resort, not the first

use_when: one unique pivot has been extracted and a specific source has to be worked
do_not_use_when: no pivot has been extracted yet
skills.manual_gate: one unique pivot is extracted and a specific source must be worked

use_when: the sink is a model, a prompt pipeline, or a serialised model format and the sub-type is already identified
do_not_use_when: the AI/IoT sub-type has not been decided by the router
skills.manual_gate: the AI/IoT sub-type is decided by the router

use_when: an obfuscated script, a PE/.NET sample, or captured C2 traffic has to be understood
do_not_use_when: the sample is a plain CTF crackme: use rev-triage
skills.manual_gate: the sample is obfuscated script, PE/.NET, or captured C2 traffic

use_when: a flag has been verified and the chain must be written down as a reusable card
do_not_use_when: the flag is still a hypothesis
